podcast.title: Alternative Term for Technopop
podcast.body: "Electro pop" is an alternative term, alongside synth pop, used to categorize the synthesizer-driven music that emerged during the later phase of the New Wave era, commonly known as Technopop. "And we're going to use the term Technopop, although some people prefer calling it synth pop or electro pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dream as an Example
podcast.body: The band Dream, in which Brian Cox played keyboards, is identified as an electro pop group from the early 1990s. "Back in the early 90s, Brian played keyboards in an electro pop band called Dream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: LMFAO's Short-Lived Success
podcast.body: The electro pop duo LMFAO scored back-to-back number one hits with "Party Rock Anthem" and "Sexy and I Know It" but were not considered imperial because their success fizzled quickly, and their hits sounded too similar, indicating a lack of enduring artistic impact. "It might seem laughable now, but the electro pop duo of Red Foo and Sky Blue topped the hot 100 twice back to back."

podcast.title: Part of Modern New Wave Definition
podcast.body: The modern understanding of New Wave, particularly concerning its historical application, often includes Electro Pop, alongside Synth Pop and Techno Pop, within the period of approximately 1978 to 1984/85.
